title: 1. Admission of a Partner
subtitle: New Profit Sharing Ratio, Sacrificing Ratio, Revaluation, Goodwill, Capital Adjustment, AS 10, AS 26 & Ind AS 38

questions.q: Admission of a new partner results in:
options: Insolvency of existing partners
Winding up of the business
Dissolution of the firm
Reconstitution of the partnership firm

questions.q: In the absence of a contract to the contrary, admitting a new partner requires:
options: Consent of all existing partners
Consent of a majority of partners
Only the senior-most partner's consent
No consent at all

questions.q: Sacrificing ratio is calculated as:
options: New ratio divided by old ratio
New ratio minus old ratio
Old ratio plus new ratio
Old ratio minus new ratio

questions.q: The sacrificing ratio is primarily used to:
options: Revalue the firm's liabilities
Calculate the new partner's capital
Distribute the goodwill brought in by the incoming partner among the old partners
Determine the firm's total capital

questions.q: If the new partner's share is given but nothing is said about how old partners sacrifice, it is assumed they sacrifice:
options: In the capital ratio
In their old profit-sharing ratio
In the new ratio
Equally

questions.q: A Revaluation Account is prepared at the time of admission to record:
options: The new partner's capital contribution
The firm's total sales
Changes in the value of assets and liabilities
The partners' drawings

questions.q: An increase in the value of an asset on revaluation is:
options: Debited to the Goodwill Account
Credited to the Revaluation Account
Credited to the new partner's capital account
Debited to the Revaluation Account

questions.q: A decrease in the value of a liability on revaluation is:
options: Debited to the Capital Accounts of all partners
Credited to the Cash Account
Credited to the Revaluation Account
Debited to the Revaluation Account

questions.q: Profit or loss on revaluation at the time of admission is shared by:
options: Only the new partner
The old partners equally, regardless of their old ratio
All partners including the new partner, in the new ratio
The old partners in their old profit-sharing ratio

questions.q: Goodwill brought in cash by a new partner is known as:
options: Sacrifice reserve
Premium for goodwill
Revaluation profit
Capital reserve

questions.q: When a new partner brings goodwill in cash, it is shared by the old partners in their:
options: Equal ratio
Sacrificing ratio
New profit-sharing ratio
Capital ratio

questions.q: Goodwill that is not explicitly given, but is inferred from the capital brought in by the new partner, is called:
options: Negative goodwill
Hidden or inferred goodwill
Super profit
Premium goodwill

questions.q: Hidden goodwill is generally calculated as:
options: The average profit of the firm
The sacrificing ratio multiplied by total capital
The implied total capitalised value of the firm minus the actual combined capital of all partners
The new partner's capital divided by the old partners' capital

questions.q: Under the Capitalisation Method, goodwill is calculated as:
options: Total assets minus total liabilities
Average profit multiplied by number of years' purchase only
Super profit multiplied by an annuity factor
Capitalised value of average profits minus the firm's net tangible assets (actual capital employed)

questions.q: Under the Super Profit Method, goodwill is generally calculated as:
options: Super profit multiplied by the agreed number of years' purchase
Average profit multiplied by total capital
Normal profit minus total assets
Capital employed divided by average profit

questions.q: Super profit is defined as:
options: Total profit of all years added together
Average profit multiplied by number of partners
Average actual profit minus normal profit
Normal profit minus average profit

questions.q: As per AS 26 (Intangible Assets), internally generated (self-generated) goodwill of a firm:
options: Must always be recorded at market value
Is treated as a current asset
Is not recognised as an asset in the books
Is compulsorily amortised over five years

questions.q: Ind AS 38, dealing with intangible assets, similarly provides that:
options: Internally generated goodwill should not be recognised as an asset
Goodwill is always amortised over its useful life
Goodwill is classified as property, plant and equipment
All goodwill must be revalued annually

questions.q: AS 10 (Property, Plant and Equipment) is relevant to admission of a partner primarily because it governs:
options: The accounting treatment of revaluation of fixed assets
The treatment of goodwill brought in cash
The preparation of the Partners' Capital Accounts only
The calculation of sacrificing ratio

questions.q: When old partners' capitals are to be adjusted in proportion to the new profit-sharing ratio, any excess capital shown by a partner is:
options: Transferred to the Goodwill Account
Withdrawn by that partner, or transferred to a loan/current account
Credited to the Revaluation Account
Written off as a loss

questions.q: Under the Fluctuating Capital Method, a partner's share of revaluation profit, goodwill adjustment and reserves is:
options: Adjusted in a separate Current Account
Ignored entirely
Adjusted directly in the partner's Capital Account
Transferred to the firm's Reserve Account

questions.q: Under the Fixed Capital Method, adjustments like share of profit, interest on capital and drawings are recorded in the:
options: Realisation Account
Partners' Capital Accounts
Partners' Current Accounts
Revaluation Account

questions.q: At the time of admission, reserves and accumulated profits appearing in the old Balance Sheet are:
options: Written off as a loss to the Revaluation Account
Distributed among the old partners in their old profit-sharing ratio
Distributed among all partners including the new partner
Carried forward unchanged in the new Balance Sheet

questions.q: If a new partner acquires their share entirely from one old partner, the sacrifice is:
options: Unequal, with only that one partner sacrificing
Equal between all old partners
Zero, since no sacrifice is needed
In proportion to capital

questions.q: The accounting entry for revaluation profit distributed to old partners is:
options: Revaluation Account debited, old partners' Capital Accounts credited in old ratio
Cash Account debited, Revaluation Account credited
Goodwill Account debited, Revaluation Account credited
Old partners' Capital Accounts debited, Revaluation Account credited

questions.q: Admission of a partner normally changes the:
options: Statutory audit requirement only
Legal status of the firm from unlimited to limited liability
Nature of the business only
Profit-sharing ratio of the partners

questions.q: Unrecorded assets discovered at the time of admission are:
options: Credited to the Revaluation Account
Credited directly to the new partner's Capital Account
Debited to the Revaluation Account
Ignored, since they were never recorded

questions.q: Unrecorded liabilities discovered at the time of admission are:
options: Ignored, since they were never recorded
Debited directly to the new partner's Capital Account
Credited to the Revaluation Account
Debited to the Revaluation Account

questions.q: A credit balance (profit) in the Revaluation Account on admission increases:
options: The firm's bank balance only
The capital account of only the new partner
The capital accounts of the old partners, in old ratio
The firm's goodwill account directly

questions.q: "Premium for goodwill" in the context of admission best refers to:
options: The amount paid by the incoming partner for the right to share future profits
The amount paid to settle a retiring partner's dues
The market value of the firm's fixed assets
The capital contributed by the incoming partner for the business

questions.q: When the new partner's share of goodwill is withdrawn in cash by the old partners, the entry debits:
options: Old partners' Capital Accounts (or a Premium for Goodwill account) and credits Cash/Bank
New partner's Capital Account and credits Cash
Cash/Bank and credits old partners' Capital Accounts
Revaluation Account and credits Cash

questions.q: Valuation of goodwill by the Average Profit Method generally computes goodwill as:
options: Super profit divided by normal rate of return
Capital employed multiplied by normal rate of return
Average profit of past years multiplied by the agreed number of years' purchase
Weighted average profit minus normal profit

questions.q: The term "number of years' purchase" in goodwill valuation represents:
options: The number of years for which a buyer is willing to pay for anticipated future profits
The number of years' capital invested by partners
The number of years the firm has been in existence
The number of years the new partner will remain a partner

questions.q: Using the new partner's capital to work out the implied total capital of the firm is an approach associated with:
options: Settling retiring partners' dues
Ascertaining hidden goodwill
Preparing the Revaluation Account
Calculating the sacrificing ratio

questions.q: Partners' Capital Accounts are adjusted after admission mainly to ensure:
options: All partners withdraw equal amounts
Goodwill is permanently retained in the books
The firm's total assets equal its total liabilities
Capitals are in proportion to the new profit-sharing ratio, where so agreed

questions.q: The Memorandum Revaluation Account method is used when:
options: Old partners do not want the recorded values of assets and liabilities to be permanently changed, despite revaluation
The new partner refuses to bring in capital
The firm is being dissolved
A partner is retiring

questions.q: In the Memorandum Revaluation Account method, the assets and liabilities in the firm's books:
options: Are transferred to the Realisation Account
Continue to appear at their old (book) values
Are written off completely
Are immediately revised to new values permanently

questions.q: Which accounting standard specifically deals with the recognition and measurement of intangible assets, including goodwill?
options: AS 6
AS 10
AS 26
AS 1

questions.q: Which accounting standard deals with Property, Plant and Equipment, including their revaluation?
options: Ind AS 38
AS 9
AS 10
AS 26

questions.q: Ind AS 38 is the Indian accounting standard that corresponds, internationally, to:
options: IAS 2 (Inventories)
IAS 38 (Intangible Assets)
IAS 16 (Property, Plant and Equipment)
IFRS 9 (Financial Instruments)

questions.q: If goodwill already appears in the old Balance Sheet at the time of admission, the usual first step is to:
options: Revalue it at twice its book value
Ignore it completely
Write it off among the old partners in their old profit-sharing ratio
Transfer it directly to the new partner's Capital Account

questions.q: The primary purpose of calculating the new profit-sharing ratio on admission is to determine:
options: The incoming partner's final dues only
The firm's total sales for the year
How all partners, including the incoming partner, will share future profits and losses
The income tax payable by the firm

questions.q: A partner's "sacrifice" on admission means that partner's share of future profits:
options: Decreases, to make room for the incoming partner's share
Is transferred entirely to the firm's reserves
Increases automatically
Remains exactly the same

questions.q: If the new profit-sharing ratio is given directly in the question (rather than the new partner's share alone), the sacrificing ratio is found by:
options: Dividing the firm's total profit by the number of partners
Comparing each old partner's old share with their new share
Ignoring the old ratio altogether
Comparing the new partner's capital with total capital

questions.q: At admission, the combined effect of revaluation and goodwill adjustments is ultimately reflected in:
options: The new partner's drawings
The firm's Profit and Loss Appropriation Account only
The partners' Capital (or Current) Accounts
The firm's statutory audit report
